newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices close higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices close higher in slow trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Thursday with buying focusing on low-priced issues and brokers expected the market to continue consolidating around current levels after the three-day holiday weekend.
The index advanced 21.85 points or 0.34 percent at 6,458.91. Turnover was T$32.79 billion. The market is closed on Friday and Saturday for domestic holidays and reopens on Monday.
Brokers noted slow sentiment following recent selling by foreign institutions and a pre-holiday mood. Most players were sidelined taking a wait-and-see attitude, they added.
"Though people largely did not want to buy, they did not want to sell either. I am not pessimistic about the outlook," said Oliver Fang of National Securities.
Late buying was seen in fundamentals-backed electronics. Most-active issue Microtek rose T$2.2 or 5.3 percent to T$43.5.
Ta Chen Stainless Pipe Co Ltd had a dazzling debut, rising the daily seven percent limit to T$26.7.
Ta Chen's celebration rally rise led a rebound in the steel sector, which had sagged in the market's recent consolidation. Tung Ho Steel ended up 30 cents or 1.1 percent to T$27.2.
The index has lost nearly 200 points since mid-October mainly because of foreign selling.
"Foreign institutions will still be a main factor for the market, but it seems they have decreased their selling in the past few days," said Clint Cheng of China Securities.

Low-priced and fundamentals-backed shares were likely to rise in turn to support the overall market but major movements in share prices were not expected due to a lack of fresh market-moving factors, brokers said.
Strong support was seen at 6,400 points while resistance was seen above 6,500 points. -- Joyce Liu (2-5080815)
